problem.original_text: Solve the initial value problem $$\frac{dy}{dx}=y(1-y), \quad y(0)=\frac{1}{2}$$. Show at least 6 steps and include a plot of $$y(x)$$ on $$[-6,6]$$.
problem.normalized_text: Solve the initial value problem $$\frac{dy}{dx}=y(1-y), \quad y(0)=\frac{1}{2}$$. Show at least 6 steps and include a plot of $$y(x)$$ on $$[-6,6]$$.

steps.title: Recognize separable ODE
steps.explanation: The equation is dy/dx = y(1-y), a separable differential equation.

steps.title: Separate variables
steps.explanation: Rewrite to put y-terms with dy and x-terms with dx.

steps.title: Integrate both sides
steps.explanation: Integrate left by partial fractions and right w.r.t. x.

steps.title: Compute integrals
steps.explanation: Integrate termwise to get logarithms plus constant.

steps.title: Solve for y
steps.explanation: Exponentiate and solve algebraically for y in terms of x.

steps.title: Apply initial condition
steps.explanation: Use y(0)=1/2 to determine C, then present final solution.

final_answer.answer_text: Unverified explanation: The solution is y(x)=1/(1+e^{-x}).
